title: mrson bulk descriptors
note: mrson never inlines bulk. A bulk-bearing field holds one of the descriptor shapes below.
This file is a DECLARATIVE FIELD TABLE, not JSON Schema: it is interpreted by both
mrson/validate.ts and mrson/validate.py so the two cannot drift. See mrson/README.md.

hash.doc: A content-addressed blob, fetched at blobBase + <this string>. Used by mesh points/triangles/normals.

doc: The LEGACY BulkRef(hash) form, named normatively by docs/MRSON-LIVESCENE.md section 2:
{ hash, dtype, count, comps, size }. Still on disk in the published gallery scenes under
live/legacy/scenes/, so it is a SUPPORTED READ form. Nothing emits it any more:
serialize_mrson.py::_mesh_blob writes the bare 'sha256-<hex>' string instead.

hash.doc: 32 lowercase hex, NOT sha256-prefixed and NOT a sha256 digest. Fetched at blobBase + <hash>, verbatim.

dtype.doc: LEGACY dtype vocabulary — plain names, NOT the NumPy-style strings zarr uses ('<f4', '|u1'). See divergence 4 in mrson/README.md.

comps.doc: components per tuple (3 for points/normals, 1 for scalars)

zarr.doc: A chunked array. Chunks are zlib-deflated, content-addressed, and stored flat under blobBase.

chunks.doc: C order (cz, cy, cx); edge chunks are zero-padded

chunkGrid.doc: number of chunks along (z, y, x)

bytes.divergence: serialize_mrson.py::_zarr_desc stringifies this ('mrson int64-safe rule'); logic/ingest.ts and serialize.py emit a number; render/zarr.ts types it as number. Both forms are accepted and normalized to a number on read; the string form warns. It is advisory, so nothing load-bearing depends on it.

chunkHashes.doc: 'k.j.i' -> blob hash. Absent only in the legacy positional layout below.

dir.doc: Legacy positional layout: chunks at blobBase + dir + '/' + dataset + '/k.j.i'.

constraints: chunkHashes OR (dir AND dataset) must be present — a reader needs some way to locate chunks.
chunkGrid[d] == ceil(shape[d] / chunks[d]) for d in 0..2.

doc: Bulk BY REFERENCE: 'this object's bulk is these DICOM instances.' Defined by
docs/MRCOM-SCENE-BUNDLE.md sections 4 and 6. Instances are named by SOPInstanceUID,
which is authoritative and archive-independent; `retrieve` entries are ordered HINTS.
A reader reconstructs, VERIFIES against `recon`, re-chunks, and replaces this descriptor
with an honest `zarr` descriptor for the bytes it actually has — it never trusts a chunk

instances.doc: Ordered SOPInstanceUIDs. The ORDER IS NORMATIVE: it is the author's geometric order, so slice order is never re-guessed.

onGridOf.doc: node id whose grid this resamples onto (dicom-seg)

reader.doc: which reconstruction algorithm produced the fields below, e.g. mrcom/dicom-series/1

voxelDigest.doc: SHA-256 of the reconstructed voxels: C order (z,y,x), post-rescale, native dtype, little-endian, unpadded. Pinned byte-for-byte in docs/MRCOM-SCENE-BUNDLE.md section 6.3.

retrieve.doc: Ordered location hints, fast path first, durable path second. Each has a `scheme`; a reader dispatches to the resolver registered for it and falls through on failure. Credentials are NEVER stored here.

doc: Where bulk descriptors legitimately appear. Anything added here must also be walked by
blobRefs() in render/sessions/session-store.ts, or the closure silently loses blobs.

legacyBlobRoles.doc: Role names seen in the published legacy scenes' `blobs` maps. Note `polys`, where the current serializer emits a flat `triangles` field — divergence 5 in mrson/README.md.

dispatch.doc: How a reader tells the four bulk shapes apart. Checked in this order.
